items.headline: Japan's economy unexpectedly shrinks in Q3 as shoppers pull back
items.caption: Japan's GDP fell 0.1% at an annual pace in July to September, when economists expected growth. It's the first drop in four quarters.

visual.title: Japan Q3 GDP, annualized
visual.foot: Reuters: prior quarter revised to 1.7% growth

detail: Japan's economy contracted 0.1% at an annualized rate in the third quarter. A Reuters poll had expected 0.3% growth. Quarter over quarter, output was basically flat.

Consumer spending, more than half the economy, fell 0.3%. Rain, typhoons, high prices and a payback after earlier car and air-conditioner buying all hurt. Business investment rose 1.6%, helped by AI and labor-saving projects. Higher energy imports took 0.6 points off growth.
The Bank of Japan has raised rates twice this year, in June and September. Its rate is 1.25%, and a move to 1.5% in December is widely expected. The dollar is pressing toward 160 yen.
money: A weak yen makes Japan trips cheaper for Americans. Watch fares and hotel deals if you plan travel.
If you own international stock funds, Japan is often one of the biggest country weights. Check your fund's mix.
Business investment in AI is still growing even as shoppers pull back, a theme showing up across many economies.
risk: Weak growth could make the BOJ delay its December hike, which could push the yen even lower.
A revised GDP estimate comes next month and could change the picture.

items.headline: Megaspeed says Alice Huang left in 2025 and hires outside lawyers to investigate
items.caption: The Singapore cloud firm at the center of the Nvidia scandal says she has no role there now. It bought over $4.8 billion of Nvidia chips in about two years.

visual.title: Megaspeed and Nvidia
visual.label: Nvidia chips Megaspeed bought in about two years, per CNBC.

detail: Megaspeed told CNBC that Alice Huang left the company at the end of August 2025 and has no current role. It has hired outside lawyers to review media reports about its business and supply chain.

The firm is suspected of buying Nvidia chips for Southeast Asian data centers and passing them to Chinese companies to dodge US limits. Megaspeed says it does business lawfully and will review its export-control compliance.
Singapore's Ministry of Home Affairs told the Wall Street Journal it did not investigate Huang. That disputes an earlier report that local authorities had probed her.
money: Nvidia reports earnings this week. Headlines like this can swing the stock, so avoid big trades on rumors.
If you own chip funds, Nvidia is often the largest holding. Know how much of your money rides on one name.
Watch whether Commerce adds Megaspeed to its blacklist. That could hit Nvidia's Asia sales.
risk: More details from the probes could move chip stocks sharply either way.

The partners are India, the UK, South Korea, the UAE, Germany, Sweden, the Netherlands and the European Commission. The registry covers semiconductors, energy infrastructure, critical minerals and the parts needed to build advanced AI.
The timing matters. Trump is set to meet Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the APEC summit this week.
money: Supply-chain pacts can steer spending toward chip, mineral and power companies in partner countries. Watch which industries get named.
If you invest in AI, know that rules and alliances, not just demand, now shape who wins.
Trade tension headlines can bring short-term dips. Steady investors sometimes use those to rebalance.

items.caption: An SF Standard investigation questions the San Francisco company's claims. GM called a claimed $300 million order relationship 'fabricated.'

visual.foot: Payroll report via CNBC, cited by SF Standard

The cofounder says the company has done over $70 million in work through prime and subcontracts. It leases its MK-1 robot for $100,000 a year per unit.

Missed payroll is a red flag. Workers can file wage claims with their state labor agency.
Public robot and AI stocks can swing on stories like this. Diversify instead of betting on one theme.

Rep. Jim Himes said Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick should be held accountable for enforcement and noted Megaspeed was not on the Entity List.
Sen. Bill Cassidy said health care costs are high and rising and small businesses are dropping coverage. He also said Social Security needs action now and pointed to his bipartisan bill.

Small business owners can look at options like individual-coverage HRAs to help staff with premiums.
Chip policy news can move Nvidia-heavy funds. Don't overreact to a single hearing.

items.headline: Canaccord Genuity's CEO moves to take the investment bank private
items.caption: A company owned by CEO Daniel Daviau would buy out other shareholders for about C$15.27 a share. The deal depends on selling its UK wealth unit.
detail: Canaccord Genuity, a Canadian investment bank, announced a proposed deal on Sunday for its chairman and CEO, Daniel Daviau, to take it private through a company he owns.

Shareholders would get C$7.45 in cash plus £4.15 converted to Canadian dollars at closing. At Friday's exchange rate, that totals about C$15.27 a share. Preferred holders would get C$25.30 plus unpaid dividends.
The deal needs court, shareholder and regulatory approvals. It also depends on the sale of the company's UK and Crown Dependencies wealth business. The value will move with the pound until closing.
money: If you hold the stock, compare the offer to the market price. The gap shows how much risk traders see in the deal.
Part of the payout is tied to the British pound, so currency moves change what you get.

items.headline: Thanksgiving travel: 81.5 million on the move, and flights cost $800 round trip
items.caption: AAA expects slightly fewer travelers than last year, ending a three-year record run. Airfares are up 17%, while gas has fallen below $4.
detail: AAA projects 81.5 million people will travel for Thanksgiving, from Tuesday, Nov. 24, through Monday, Nov. 30. That's about 121,000 fewer than last year and ends three straight record years. AAA partly blames fuel costs.

The average domestic round-trip fare is $800, up 17%. Gas averaged $3.94 on Nov. 11, down from $4.36 a month earlier but well above last year's $3.07. GasBuddy says prices could slip into the high $3s by the holiday.
Orlando, Fort Lauderdale and Miami top the domestic list. The worst traffic is expected Tuesday and Wednesday before the holiday, and on the return Sunday and Monday.
money: Leave early on Tuesday or travel on Thanksgiving morning to dodge the worst traffic.
With fares up 17%, compare the cost of driving for trips under about 500 miles.
Use a gas app to find cheaper stations. Prices may keep falling into the holiday.
risk: Flight disruptions this month show delays can spread fast. Know your refund rights before you fly.

items.headline: Tesla opens Cybercab orders at $29,990, but it needs a $299-a-month plan
items.caption: Select customers can buy the no-steering-wheel robotaxi for personal use. It only works in supported areas, and deliveries could start next month.
detail: Tesla began inviting select customers to order the Cybercab for personal use at $29,990, about $7,000 less than a Model 3. Owners must pay $299 a month for an autonomous driving subscription, about $3,600 a year.
The two-seater has no steering wheel, pedals or side mirrors. It can operate only in supported service areas, not nationwide. Deliveries could begin as soon as next month.
Federal safety regulators are asking how Tesla decided the car meets safety standards. Cars that don't comply can be deployed only under an exemption capped at 2,500 a year.
money: Add up the true cost: $29,990 plus about $3,600 a year, plus insurance and upkeep.
If you live outside a service area, the car can't drive you anywhere yet.
Tesla investors should watch how many units actually reach buyers versus Tesla's own fleet.
risk: Regulators could limit how many are sold.
Early tech cars can lose value fast.

items.headline: Philadelphia: 36,000 lost SNAP, and 70,000 more could lose Medicaid in 2027
items.caption: Federal changes are now hitting city residents. Democrats take Congress in January but likely can't fully reverse the cuts.

rows.k: PA SNAP cost by next Oct.

detail: About 36,000 Philadelphians have lost SNAP food aid since new eligibility rules took effect in September 2025, the Inquirer reports. Statewide, SNAP enrollment fell about 239,000.

Starting Jan. 1, the federal government will focus on about 183,000 city residents who joined Medicaid through the ACA expansion. State officials say more than 70,000 could lose coverage. Up to 300,000 Pennsylvanians could be removed statewide.

Democrats take control of Congress in January, but repeal bills would likely face a veto. Ideas include tying ICE funding to offsetting Medicaid cuts. A Senate farm bill would delay the state SNAP cost share by a year.
money: If you get Medicaid or SNAP, respond quickly to any renewal or work-hours notice. Missing paperwork is a top reason people lose aid.
Keep pay stubs and proof of work, school or volunteering hours in one place.
If you lose Medicaid, check ACA marketplace plans right away. You may qualify for help paying premiums.
risk: Rules vary by state and are still changing, so check your state's benefits website.

items.headline: After midterm wins, Democrats push minimum wage hikes; economists warn of job cuts
items.caption: Pennsylvania's governor wants $15, Illinois' governor is urging a federal raise, and Hakeem Jeffries says $7.25 must go up. Critics warn of fewer hours.
detail: Democrats are using their midterm wins to push for higher minimum wages. Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro wants to more than double the state's $7.25 rate to $15. Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker is calling on Congress to raise the federal minimum. House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries says it needs to rise.

Economists at the American Institute for Economic Research and the Illinois Policy Institute warn steep hikes could lead small businesses to raise prices, cut hours or slow hiring, especially for young and entry-level workers.
Research is mixed. One study of Seattle found higher pay but fewer hours for less experienced workers. A Berkeley study found no significant drop in restaurant jobs.
money: If you earn near the minimum, track your state's bills. A raise could change your budget next year.
Business owners should plan for higher labor costs now, not after a law passes.
Workers getting raises should check whether higher income affects benefits like SNAP or Medicaid.
risk: A federal raise still faces a likely veto; state action is more likely.

detail: Brent crude fell about 2.5% last week, its second weekly loss in a row. The International Energy Agency says the oil market has swung back to a surplus as Gulf exports recover, and US stockpiles rose.
Iran said three tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday. The US military disputes that and says the main lanes are clear. Traders will price those claims as futures reopen Sunday night.
Next up: the government's weekly oil inventory report Wednesday, then a full OPEC+ meeting Nov. 29 that sets 2027 output. Talk of pumping more could push prices lower.
money: Lower crude usually reaches the gas pump within a few weeks, so it can pay to hold off on topping up a full tank at high prices.
Airline and trucking stocks tend to gain when fuel costs fall.
If you heat with oil, compare pre-buy plans now while prices are near their lowest since August.

The Financial Times reported that lead banks Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley weighed pricing above the range because of strong demand. A higher price or a raised range would be a sign of heat; nothing is final until Wednesday.
The company reported a $104 billion net loss for the first nine months, mostly from a one-time, non-cash charge of $94.3 billion. Its co-founders keep voting control through a special share.

If you already own index funds, you'll likely get some exposure once ANT joins major indexes, without picking a price.
Waiting a few weeks after a hot IPO often gives a calmer entry point.

A former Meta employee who writes a newsletter on early retirement estimates senior engineers' yearly stock pay could fall more than 40% once the old grants run out. That could push some to retire early or leave.
Meta recently cut about 700 jobs and gave stock options to six top executives, its first such grants since its 2012 IPO. Meta hasn't said how it will replace the expiring value.

Holding too much of your employer's stock is risky; many planners suggest spreading out after vesting.

items.headline: Debt-free and earning six figures, but denied credit: the thin-file problem
items.caption: Card debt hit a record $1.29 trillion, yet some high earners with no debt get rejected. Scoring models reward recent account activity, not income or savings.

visual.title: Credit by the numbers
visual.label: US credit card balances, up 67% since early 2021 (NY Fed).

detail: Fox Business reports that automated lending systems are turning down some people with big salaries, no debt and solid savings. The reason: their credit files are too thin or too old to produce a normal score.
The CFPB estimates about 25 million adults are in that spot. Credit scores track how you handle borrowed money, so paying cash for everything can leave little to score.
Experts split on the fix. One camp says keep a card or two with tiny charges paid off monthly. Another says skip debt and build a 3-to-6-month cash cushion.
money: Put one small recurring bill on a card and pay it in full each month to keep your file active at no cost.
Don't close your oldest card; account age helps your score.
A good score can save thousands on a mortgage or car loan through lower rates.
risk: Carrying a balance costs interest; only use cards you can pay off in full.
Buy now, pay later loans can lower your average account age.

items.headline: Montana's governor wants a 4.7% flat income tax and a bigger EITC
items.caption: Gov. Gianforte's next budget would flatten the income tax at 4.7% and lift the state earned income credit to 30% of the federal one. Democrats say the rich gain most.

visual.title: Gianforte's budget asks
visual.foot: Proposals for the 2027 Legislature

detail: Montana Gov. Greg Gianforte released budget priorities for the 2027 legislative session. The plan would move the state to a single 4.7% income tax rate. He says the top rate has already dropped from 6.9% and brackets went from seven to two.

The state's earned income tax credit for working families would rise from 20% to 30% of the federal credit. Small businesses could exempt up to $3 million of equipment from property tax, up from $1 million.
The plan also puts $300 million into the rainy day fund and $225 million into state and county roads. Senate Republican leaders back the flat tax; House Democrats oppose it.
money: Montana workers who get the federal EITC could see a bigger state credit if it passes.
Business owners with equipment between $1M and $3M could save on property tax.
Track your state's legislature this winter: tax changes often apply to the next tax year.

Australia's ambassador argued that curbs would raise prices for US shoppers.

Chicken and pork are usually cheaper protein swaps if lamb prices jump.
US sheep ranchers could see better prices if imports are limited.

Rehabilitation or consolidation can bring a loan back to good standing; ask your servicer which fits.

items.headline: AI race: Google’s Gemini 4 Carbon takes #1, Tencent drops a giant open model
items.caption: Gemini 4 Carbon topped the LMArena leaderboard. Tencent released Hy4, a 770-billion-parameter open-weights model. OpenAI says ChatGPT search is now a fifth of Google’s volume.
detail: Gemini 4 Carbon took the top spot on the LMArena text leaderboard with a rating of 1528. OpenAI released LifeVal, a benchmark that measures how well models handle practical tasks such as government paperwork and vehicle inspections.
Tencent’s Hy4 is an open-weights mixture-of-experts model with 770 billion parameters and a one-million-token context window, part of a wave of cheaper models squeezing AI prices.
On the policy side, China said it is speeding up laws to oversee algorithms and computing power, while in the US the new Democratic majority has spooked investors about data-center rules.
money: Open-weights models keep pushing AI costs down; if you pay for AI tools in a side business, shop around every few months.
Skills that combine AI with a niche (reselling listings, video editing, paperwork) are where freelancers are getting paid.
Using AI more is not the same as AI stocks going up: this week usage grew while chip stocks fell.
risk: Leaderboards change weekly; avoid locking into one paid tool long-term.

items.headline: Bankruptcy watch: franchise operators keep cracking
items.caption: A 30-restaurant Denny’s operator, a Mattress Firm franchisee and candy brand Stuckey’s all filed for Chapter 11. High rents and softer spending are squeezing small chains.
detail: EYM Diner, which runs about 30 Denny’s restaurants in Texas, is the latest bankruptcy tied to former mega-franchisee EYM Group. D&A Mattress, a Mattress Firm franchisee in Texas and New Mexico, filed on November 2.

Franchise operators have filed in clusters throughout 2026, citing high lease costs, weaker spending on non-essentials and tighter credit. Bain expects global luxury sales to shrink for a second straight year.
Chapter 11 lets a company keep operating while it restructures; Stuckey’s says its brand will continue.
money: Liquidation and closing sales can be a source of cheap inventory for resellers; watch local auction and liquidation listings.
Use gift cards from struggling chains soon; they can lose value in bankruptcy.
Rising franchise failures are an early signal of consumer stress, a reason to favor steadier companies.
risk: Restructured companies can still liquidate later.

items.headline: Also on the IPO calendar: a cavity-treatment maker and a biotech
items.caption: vVardis, which sells an over-the-counter cavity treatment, and Rezera, an inflammation-drug developer, aim to raise about $200M each. New issues are down 4% this year.

rows.s: Insiders free to sell this week

detail: vVardis plans to raise about $214 million at a market value near $1.3 billion; most of its revenue comes from its over-the-counter US product. Rezera’s lead drug, ruvonoflast, heads into Phase 3 trials in the first half of 2027.
Newly public stocks have lagged: the Renaissance IPO Index was down 4.0% for the year as of November 5, while the S&P 500 was up 8.4%.
Nine lock-up periods expire this week, which can add selling pressure to recent IPOs.
money: Small biotech IPOs are binary bets on trial results; size any position as money you can afford to lose.
Check lock-up calendars before buying a recent IPO; prices often sag around expiration.
An IPO ETF spreads risk across many new listings instead of betting on one.
risk: Price ranges can change or deals can be postponed in a volatile market.
